title: Mexico Increases Seizures of Drugs and Money
author: Aníbal García Fernández
content:
_This article by[Aníbal García
Fernández](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anibal/) originally appeared in
the [October 13, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/mexico-aumenta-
decomisos-de-droga-y-dinero/), Mexico's leading investigative journalism
magazine._

_The Second Government Report highlights coordinated government actions to
combat drug trafficking, such as the seizure of hundreds of kilograms of drugs
and cash, the increase in tax collection at Customs of 526,033.69 million
pesos, and blows to criminal structures worth close to 340 million pesos.
These efforts contrast with the view of the United States government that
Mexico must do more_

On October 12, members of the Secretariat of the Navy seized a vessel with 46
bundles containing approximately 1.2 tons of presumed cocaine and arrested six
people, approximately 366 nautical miles south of Huatulco, Oaxaca. The
operation had the collaboration of the United States Coast Guard, which
provided the information.

Despite the narrative of the opposition and of the conservative government of
Donald Trump that drug trafficking prevails in Mexico and that more actions
are lacking on the part of the government of President Claudia Sheinbaum to
combat organized crime, the _Second Government Report_ allows a closer look at
the various efforts to address the different causes of violence.

For example, blows to drug trafficking equivalent to close to 340 million
pesos stand out. This amount is for the seizure of five aircraft, three
vehicles, and 1,224 kilograms of cocaine, to which the most recent seizure is
added.

In addition to the above, the Security Cabinet reported that from October 2024
to September 30, 2026, more than 70,500 people were arrested for high-impact
crimes; 36,300 firearms and 569 tons of drugs have been seized, and 2,792
clandestine laboratories for the production of synthetic drugs were
dismantled.

At the presidential press conference on October 13, it was detailed that 2,170
people related to this crime have also been arrested in 24 states of the
country since the implementation of the National Strategy against Extortion.

The Secretary of Security and Citizen Protection, Omar García Harfuch,
highlighted that the national daily average of intentional homicides decreased
by 52 percent, which means 45 fewer homicides each day.

### Strengthening of Customs and Benito Juárez Airport

Part of President Sheinbaum’s strategy is to strengthen surveillance and
security at customs through a comprehensive strategy.**The Secretariat of
Defense (Sedena) assigned 2,663 military personnel to provide permanent
support to the National Customs Agency of Mexico** (ANAM) at the 32 customs
offices it coordinates. The presence of Sedena personnel resulted in the
arrest of 369 people, 141 weapons seized, 141,841 cartridges, 899 magazines,
419 vehicles, 839,540 Mexican pesos, and 3,050,491 dollars. Also the seizure
of 36.2 kilograms of marijuana, 133.8 kilograms of cocaine, 109.6 kilograms of
methamphetamine, and 737,300 liters of hydrocarbons as well as 6.7 liters of
chemical precursors.

The _Second Report_ also mentions the collection of 526,033.69 million pesos
raised through the efforts of Defense personnel in support of ANAM.

The Secretariat of the Navy (Semar) also participates in strengthening customs
with the installation of non-intrusive inspection equipment. In maritime
customs, 80 percent of this equipment has been installed. In ports, 37,317
dollars, six firearm magazines, 513 live cartridges, 184.8 kilograms of
methamphetamine, 17.9 kilograms of marijuana, and 34.9 kilograms of cocaine
have been seized. **Due to the collaboration between ANAM and Semar, customs
revenue of 35,657.9 million pesos was produced from September 1, 2025 to June
30, 2026**.

For its part, **at Benito Juárez Airport in Mexico City, 335,885 kilograms of
illicit substances were seized** (it is not indicated whether they are drugs),
1,233 rounds of ammunition and six firearms, 543,422 kilograms of sea
cucumber, and 264 specimens of exotic animals. In addition, 22 Mexican and
seven foreign people were arrested and placed at the disposal of the Attorney
General’s Office (FGR).

### Comprehensive North American Maritime Shield and Regional Cooperation

An area little explored by certain security experts, and by the concepts of
militarism-militarization in Mexico, is that of the training courses received
by the Mexican armed forces. The training courses are part of the bilateral
relationship between the United States and Mexico, and most of the armed
forces are trained at military centers in that country.

The training courses are part of a transfer of technology, knowledge,
interests, ways of thinking, and military practices on civilian problems. It
implies a set of geopolitical interests transferred to other military
institutions.[1]

According to the _Second Government Report_ , 518 members of the Mexican army
participated in the 2026 Rotational Exercise together with Northern Command.
Between September and October 2025, the armed forces participated in the
Multinational Exercise “UNITAS” at the Naval Bases of Mayport, Florida, and
Norfolk, Virginia, USA. The purpose of the exercise was “to strengthen
interoperability and cooperation with the participating armed forces of South
America, through combined training in naval, amphibious, and security
operations.”

Already in 2026, Sedena reports the first exercise in San Diego, California,
within the framework of the North American Maritime Security Initiative
(NAMSI). This initiative was made public on June 6, although it dates back to
2008, in the time of Felipe Calderón, who accepted foreign interference in the
country. Mexico, within the framework of respect for sovereignty, tested the
effectiveness of the naval trinomial model, made up of a ship, helicopter, and
interceptor patrol boat, as well as the incorporation of “unmanned systems
that have significantly expanded surveillance capabilities.”

What the report does not mention is that with NAMSI the binational SAREX
exercises were reactivated to “increase the specialized training of naval
personnel and expand [the] interoperability mechanism.” Also the
implementation of the SAROPS 4.5 technological system in coordination with the
United States Coast Guard to optimize search and location times for people,
vessels, and aircraft.

In March 2026, a second military exercise was held in Veracruz with the United
States and Canada. In that same month, the “Cyber Libertad” exercise was held,
with 12 Mexican naval personnel. And existing cooperation was strengthened in
port infrastructure protection, academic cooperation, cybersecurity,
specialized training, interoperability, and joint exercises.

It is important to mention that NAMSI also includes Canada. According to
Northern Command, “the meeting culminated with the formal signing of the
revised NAMSI Manual by the Heads of Delegation, which establishes updated
standard operating procedures that allow the effective application of
international provisions, in order to strengthen the exchange of information
to combat unlawful acts against the safety of maritime navigation.”

Relations with Central America were also strengthened. For the first time, the
military exercise “LAMANAI 2025” was held from September 1 to 5, 2025, in
Ladyville, Belize. The National Center for Surveillance and Protection of
Airspace of the Joint Staff of National Defense and the Joint Intelligence and
Operations Center of Belize participated in this exercise.

Finally, Semar participated in the Inter-American Drug Abuse Control
Commission, a body that is part of the Organization of American States (OAS),
with which work is being done on the document “**Hemispheric Plan of Action on
Drugs 2026-2030** ,” in which it participated in three consultation events on
the plan. **Mexico proposed that the Plan consider a public health approach,
with social prevention policies over coercion mechanisms.** Since November
2025, Semar has sent comments and opinions on said Plan to the Secretariat of
Foreign Affairs (SRE).

### Professionalization of the National Guard

One of the relevant points that the _Second Report_ highlights is the
continuity and professionalization of the National Guard. In other
administrations, it was customary for federal police forces to be modified
almost every six-year term: so it was with Ernesto Zedillo and the Federal
Preventive Police, and the creation of the Federal Police under Felipe
Calderón, and later under Enrique Peña the Secretariat of Public Security was
eliminated, the Federal Police passed to the Secretariat of Governance, and
the Gendarmerie was formed.

With the two Morena governments, continuity is given to **the National Guard,
now made up of 115,979 members, of whom 109,110 belong to the Public Security
Force and 3,829 to the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection.**

To address public security, **the GN has a permanent deployment of 100,848
personnel throughout the country, that is, 92 percent of the total public
security force.** The firepower of the **GN is made up of 254,823 weapons** ,
of which 107,092 are handguns, 111,348 long guns, and 36,383 of other types,
as well as 33 aircraft and 21,909 vehicles of different characteristics.

Regarding its professionalization, from September 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026,
523 members graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree in Public Security from the
Heroic Military College and the Air College, and 1,176 personnel as sergeants
specializing in public security from the Military School of Classes of the
Arms of the Military Police Service and the National Guard. In addition,
43,117 personnel were trained in 1,438 academic activities in basic and
specialized skills.

**The results of the GN are 1,763 people linked to criminal acts, seizures in
102 events** , 78 percent of which were concentrated in six states: Sinaloa
(19 percent), Mexico City (18 percent), Morelos (12 percent), the State of
Mexico and Puebla (11 percent each), and Michoacán (7 percent).
